newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Ramco to reverse JKX fortunes.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Ramco to reverse JKX fortunes.

text.p: Oil exploration firm Ramco Energy Plc promised a major shake-up at bid target JKX Oil & Gas to reverse the latter's ill-fated fortunes in Ukraine.
Ramco's chief executive Steve Remp said he sought to drastically cut costs at JKX and wanted to bring in a major Western energy group to boost JKX's Ukrainian gas operations.
Preliminary talks with a potential partner have already taken place.
In an interview with Reuters, Remp was highly critical of JKX's spending in the past and its previous strategy of going it alone.
He said Ramco's 54 million stg agreed bid offered JKX shareholders the best chance to make up for the losses posted on their investments.
"The Ramco shareholders have done pretty well and the JKX shareholders have done particularly badly," Remp said.
"The case I bring directly to shareholders is that they have the best chance to redress and make up for their past losses by coming on board with us," he added.
Ramco has already received irrevocable undertakings to accept the offer from institutional investors who together have a 26 percent interest in JKX.
Remp has been widely credited for Ramco's pioneering role in Azerbaijan, where it helped bring together Western oil majors to revive the offshore oil industry in the Caspian Sea.

The plan for a JKX take-over was put to Remp by investment bankers UBS a couple of months ago. Remp said the time for the acquisition was right as he believed the Ukraine saw the need to reorganise its gas market.
The country cannot afford to import about 90 percent of its gas at over twice the contract rates for gas produced by JKX, Remp said.
JKX is active in the Ukraine gas market through 49 percent-owned Poltava Petroleum Company (PPC).
JKX fell on hard times last year when the buyer of PPC's gas could no longer operate as a distributor after the Ukraine decided only domestic firms were allowed to sell gas to end-users.
While Ukraine now sees it badly needs Western investment, it also realises JKX's experiences have done little to tempt European and North American firms to enter the country, Remp said.
He therefore believed the Ukraine was keen to help Ramco in turning round JKX's operations.
"JKX has had a lot of problems and because the company has been so high profile, I think it is something of a considerable embarrassment to the Ukrainian leadership," Remp said.
"There is momentum building up to change that. There is a feeling at the highest level of government that JKX needs to perform as a signal to Western investors," he added.
Ramco wants to expand PPC's gas operations in Ukraine, while it also wants to strengthen operations in Georgia where both Ramco and JKX are already active.
Remp declined to say whether Ramco will close JKX's headquarters if the bid is successful, nor did he want to discuss the future position of JKX's board members.
JKX is being led by chief executive Bob McCrackin, who took over the helm in February and who immediately started a cost cutting operation.
"The problem with JKX historically is that they raised a lot of money from shareholders. They spent a lot of money and that's not the way we've operated in the past," said Remp.
"The management have gone a certain way addressing these past problems but I imagine we will go a lot further than that," he added.
-- Hans de Jongh, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
